exercise.name: Barbell Deadlift

reference.title: Barbell Deadlift
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page text could not be fetched from this environment)

exercise.bodyPart: Hips (glutes) and back of the thighs

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace before the bar leaves the floor, hold the brace through the pull, breathe out at the top or once the plates are back on the floor.
breathing.cadence: About 1.8 s up, a short lockout, about 2 s down, reset on the floor

prescription.tempo: Controlled pull, short lockout, controlled lowering; reset each rep on the floor
prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can pull with a flat back for every rep, leaving about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8).
prescription.progression: Add 2.5-5 kg when every rep of every set stays flat-backed and smooth off the floor.

cues.text: Bar over the middle of the foot, feet about hip width. Hinge down and grip the bar just outside the knees, overhand, arms straight. Shins to the bar, hips above the knees, shoulders just in front of the bar, back flat. Big breath and brace.
Push the floor away: the bar slides up the shins, hips and shoulders rising together; once it passes the knees drive the hips forward.
Stand tall with the hips and knees straight, shoulders over the bar; don't lean back.
Push the hips back first with the bar close to the thighs, then bend the knees once it passes them.
Set the plates down softly on the floor, keep the brace or take a new breath, then pull again.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back off the floor
mistakes.fix: Brace before the pull and take the slack out of the bar (pull it against the plates) before it leaves the floor; lower the load if the back still rounds.

mistakes.mistake: Bar drifting away from the legs
mistakes.fix: Keep the bar touching or brushing the shins and thighs; pull it toward you with straight arms.
Push with the legs so the hips and shoulders rise at the same rate until the bar passes the knees.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back hard at the top
mistakes.fix: Finish by squeezing the glutes and standing tall; the shoulders stack over the hips.
Arms stay straight like ropes; the legs and hips do the lifting.

kinematics.norm: Less knee bend than a hex-bar or dumbbell deadlift because the bar is in front of the shins (Swinton 2011)
Hips above the knees and below the shoulders at the start (clinical opinion); the conventional style starts with the hips higher and the trunk more inclined than the sumo style (Escamilla 2002)
Trunk more inclined than in a hex-bar deadlift (Swinton 2011; Stewart 2008)
Bar starts over mid-foot and travels nearly straight up, close to the legs (common coaching)
Controlled lift and lowering; reset on the floor between reps (clinical opinion)

sources.title: Escamilla et al. 2002, an electromyographic analysis of sumo and conventional style deadlifts (Med Sci Sports Exerc 34(4):682-688; PubMed 11932579)
Swinton et al. 2011, a biomechanical analysis of straight and hexagonal barbell deadlifts using submaximal loads (J Strength Cond Res 25(7):2000-2009)
Stewart & Stewart-Menteth 2008, comparative kinematic analysis of the deadlift with an Olympic bar and a Troy-Hex bar (J Sports Sci 26(2))
Lee et al. 2018, an electromyographic and kinetic comparison of conventional and Romanian deadlifts (J Exerc Sci Fit; PMC6323186)

cautions: Learn the hip hinge with a light bar or a dowel before loading up; keep the back flat on every rep.
Use plates of standard diameter (or blocks) so the bar starts at about mid-shin height.
Lower the bar under control; don't drop it from lockout.
Low-back pain: stop and get advice; pull from blocks to shorten the range until it settles.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Tight hamstrings or hips: pull from blocks or plates on risers.
Grip failing before the legs: use chalk or straps for the top sets.
regressions: Rack pull from just below the knees.
progressions: Pause just off the floor or at the knees.
Deficit deadlift from a low platform.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Main hip extensor, driving the hips through to lockout (Escamilla 2002).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Main hip extensor, driving the hips through to lockout (Escamilla 2002).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Extend the hip from the hinged start; conventional and Romanian deadlifts both loaded them heavily (Lee 2018).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Extend the hip from the hinged start; conventional and Romanian deadlifts both loaded them heavily (Lee 2018).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the back flat against the bar hanging in front; the conventional style relies on them more than the sumo style (Escamilla 2002).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the back flat against the bar hanging in front; the conventional style relies on them more than the sumo style (Escamilla 2002).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Straighten the knees to break the bar off the floor (Escamilla 2002).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Straighten the knees to break the bar off the floor (Escamilla 2002).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus assists hip extension from the bottom.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus assists hip extension from the bottom.
muscleNotes.core: Bracing stiffens the trunk so the hips and legs can move the bar.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Part of the brace around the trunk.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Part of the brace around the trunk.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Keep the bar close to the legs and the shoulders set.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Keep the bar close to the legs and the shoulders set.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Hold the shoulders against the pull of the bar on straight arms.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Hold the shoulders against the pull of the bar on straight arms.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Keep the upper back tight and the shoulder blades from being pulled apart.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Keep the upper back tight and the shoulder blades from being pulled apart.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Hold the bar; grip is often the first limit.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Hold the bar; grip is often the first limit.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Keep the whole foot pressed into the floor.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Keep the whole foot pressed into the floor.
